STAGE 1

Write the whole-module specification

InputClean module RTL: stage1/design.v
InstructionDescribe the interface, parameters, and observable behavior of this clean design. Return a self-contained specification, not RTL implementation code. A separate isolated call will receive your specification.

Stored wording: stage1/TASK.md

OutputGenerated whole-module specification (prose).
Read input: stage1/design.v · Open raw
module origen_003971 #(
    parameter W_ADDR = 12,
    parameter W_DATA = 128
)(
    // RAM interface
    output [W_ADDR-1:0] ram_rd_addr,
    output [W_ADDR-1:0] ram_wr_addr,
    output [W_DATA-1:0] ram_wr_data,
    output ram_rd_en,
    output ram_wr_en,
    input [W_DATA-1:0] ram_rd_data,

    // DMA interface
    output [W_DATA-1:0] dma_rd_data,
    input [W_ADDR-1:0] dma_rd_addr,
    input [W_ADDR-1:0] dma_wr_addr,
    input [W_DATA-1:0] dma_wr_data,
    input dma_rd_en,
    input dma_wr_en,

    // Custom interface
    output custom_en,
    output [W_DATA-1:0] custom_rd_data,
    input [W_ADDR-1:0] custom_rd_addr,
    input [W_ADDR-1:0] custom_wr_addr,
    input [W_DATA-1:0] custom_wr_data,
    input custom_rd_en,
    input custom_wr_en
);

    // DMA activity signal
    wire dma_active = dma_rd_en | dma_wr_en;

    // Custom interface enable
    assign custom_en = ~dma_active;

    // RAM read address multiplexer
    assign ram_rd_addr = dma_active ? dma_rd_addr :
                         custom_en ? custom_rd_addr : {W_ADDR{1'bx}};

    // RAM write address multiplexer
    assign ram_wr_addr = dma_active ? dma_wr_addr :
                         custom_en ? custom_wr_addr : {W_ADDR{1'bx}};

    // RAM write data multiplexer
    assign ram_wr_data = dma_active ? dma_wr_data :
                         custom_en ? custom_wr_data : {W_DATA{1'bx}};

    // RAM read enable
    assign ram_rd_en = dma_rd_en | (custom_en & custom_rd_en);

    // RAM write enable
    assign ram_wr_en = dma_wr_en | (custom_en & custom_wr_en);

    // Read data routing
    assign dma_rd_data = ram_rd_data;
    assign custom_rd_data = ram_rd_data;

endmodule

Complete the module

InputThe generated Stage 1 text plus masked module rtl: stage2_template/design.v. Required top module: origen_003971.
InstructionRestore the masked expression in design.v using the specification and retained RTL context. Return the complete corrected RTL with the same top module. Only the default configuration is scored.

Stored wording: stage2_template/TASK.md

OutputComplete RTL module with the masked logic restored.

                         custom_en ? custom_wr_data : {W_DATA{1'bx}};

    // RAM read enable

    // RAM write enable
    assign ram_wr_en = dma_wr_en | (custom_en & custom_wr_en);

    // Read data routing

    assign custom_rd_data = ram_rd_data;

endmodule

entry_point:
Agent entry point — start here

Round-trip tasks have two separate agent entry points:

  1. Stage 1: stage1/TASK.md
  2. Stage 2: stage2_template/TASK.md

Follow the stage panels below for each stage’s input files and required output. The accepted Stage 1 text is supplied to a fresh Stage 2 context; Stage 2 does not receive clean RTL or the Stage 1 conversation.

These links are the whole-module case-package instructions. The specialist/targeted view instead uses runner-generated masked-region prompts, shown in its stage panels.

A stored instruction is distinct from the runtime launch message, which can add framing and execution limits. The agent uses the harness’s file-reading tools to inspect available inputs. The file list also includes human-review reference and oracle assets that must not be given to the evaluated agent.
